title: OpenRouter Launches Armor to Block Unauthorized AI Agent Tool Calls
summary:
A new beta tool from OpenRouter uses decision models to intercept unauthorized actions by AI agents before they interact with external systems. Called Armor, the product operates as an "auto" permissions mode compatible with any AI model or harness, utilizing a specialized classifier to replace traditional regex-based filtering that the company describes as insufficient for detecting complex policy violations.

The system is powered by Typesafe AI's Jev model. Internal testing by OpenRouter found that Jev 1.13 achieved higher accuracy and lower costs than other available decision models and the classifier employed by Claude Code's Sonnet 5. The beta release aims to provide a scalable guardrail for autonomous agents executing tool calls in real-world environments.

Today, we are launching OpenRouter Armor in beta.

Tool calls allow agents to interact with the world, and regex-based filtering often isn't enough to detect unwanted tool calls.

Armor uses @typesafeai's Jev model to guard against out of policy tool calls before your agent executes them, with better performance than Claude Code's auto classifier at a fraction of the cost.
